title: Embedding pipeline tail-latency heatmap and opportunistic merge optimizations
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: We are seeing sporadic tail spikes on the embeddings endpoint (p99 and above) that disproportionately affect small-batch interactive workloads. This ticket scopes an investigation and targeted mitigations focused on: 1) building a per-model kernel heatmap and kernel-selection heuristic, 2) adding an opportunistic micro-batch merging path in the request dispatcher, and 3) improving trace sampling/observability to isolate scheduling vs kernel stalls.

Background: Production dashboards show a stable p50/p95 but p99/p999 spikes at times of bursty traffic (e.g. demo traffic and small fan-out requests). Initial traces indicate three root causes: cache misses causing extra KV re-insertions, suboptimal kernel selection for short sequences leading to kernel launch overheads, and serialization in the dispatcher when many tiny requests arrive concurrently.

Goals: Reduce p99 from baseline (~240ms) to <=120ms for the 256-dim embed model under interactive traffic; lower p999 spikes by at least 30%. Do this while keeping p50/p95 within +/-10% and not regressing throughput for large-batch customers.

Non-Goals: End-to-end reranking quality changes are out of scope; model architecture changes are not part of this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: p99 for interactive embedding workload (synthetic small-batch generator) drops to <=120ms over 1h steady-state test
p999 spike amplitude reduced by at least 30% on the same test harness
No >5% regression on throughput for 8k-batch embedding jobs in the dedicated pool
Heatmap instrumentation exposes per-model kernel selection distribution and is available in Grafana/Tempo dashboards
Opportunistic micro-batch merge is guarded by feature flag and has an AB test plan
tasks: Add fine-grained kernel telemetry (kernel_id, seq_len_bucket, input_size, launch_time) to the runtime
Build offline kernel-heatmap job that consumes traces and outputs per-model kernel recommendations
Implement opportunistic micro-batch merging in dispatcher with per-tenant rate/timeout heuristics
Add adaptive timeout that favors merging for <8-token requests during burst windows
Run A/B on canary nodes with merged-path enabled behind feature flag
Document rollback criteria and add automated fallback to previous kernel selection
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Spike analysis - collected 24h of traces (Tempo) and identified that ~62% of p99 cases used Kernel-A on seq_len<=16 where Kernel-B would have lower latency
2025-02-13: Instrumentation PR opened (runtime#9876) adding kernel_id and seq_len_bucket to traces; landed on staging
2025-02-15: Heatmap job prototype running in batch - initial output shows model=embed-small prefers Kernel-B at seq<=32 during cold cache
2025-02-17: Opportunistic merge prototype implemented in dispatcher; local microbench shows median latency unchanged, p99 improved by ~18% in synthetic burst test
2025-02-20: Canary rollout planned for 10% of traffic tomorrow; experiment dashboard and rollback playbook ready
comments: PM (Jonas Keller) 2025-02-12: Please include customer-facing regression checks; we have a pilot customer with strict SLAs for dedicated pools.
Design (Maya Patel) 2025-02-14: UX note - no changes needed to API but add a console flag to visualize kernel heatmaps per model for platform operators.
SRE (Liam O'Connor) 2025-02-16: Watch out for increased GPU kernel churn which may affect power draw; recommend adding a 1s cooldown per GPU for kernel swaps.
Reviewer (Priya Nair) 2025-02-18: Suggest tuning the merge timeout based on queue build-up rate rather than a fixed threshold; otherwise looks good.
next_steps: 01. Run 24h canary at 10% traffic with opportunistic merge + kernel-heatmap-driven selection
02. Evaluate A/B results against acceptance criteria and collect failure traces for any p99 regressions
03. If canary passes, plan a staged rollout to 50%->100% with metrics gating
04. Post-rollout: schedule a follow-up ticket to generalize heuristics across other embed sizes and quantized models
